title: canary fallback timeline and shell traces
content:
Top-level intent: quick scratchpad for the canary fallback event on 2026-03-09 — capture commands I ran, raw snippets, hypotheses so we don't lose context. Informal; use as a memory dump for postmortem.

Short summary
- ~09:37 UTC on 2026-03-09 a subset of requests from eu-west-1 customers dropped into a canary that should have been isolated. Canary routing then triggered a multi-region fallback to us-east-1. Result: increased latency and a small spike in 5xxs (~0.6% global increase) for ~12m.
- Suspect: mis-evaluated routing policy at the LB layer combined with stale canary weight in the rollout config. Also saw a KV-cache warmup mismatch when fallback chose a quantized variant of the model.

Initial observations (live)
- Grafana: spike in route-level latency for route /v1/chat/generate starting 09:37:11 UTC.
- Canary metric: canary-rolling-weight metric had value 0.12 when it should have been 0.0 for that canary (we're mid-rollout). The expected behavior was to keep 0 until traffic validation finished.
- Error signatures: mostly 502/504 at the edge, plus internal model-serve timeouts logged as "kv-cache-miss + cold-start" in the runtime logs.

Commands I ran (local host machine, session id: ash-debug-03)
- curl to reproduce client request
  curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-chat","input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/chat

  Observed (truncated):
  > GET /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
  < HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
  < Retry-After: 1
  < x-routing-decision: eu-west-1->canary-3
  < x-fallback: us-east-1

- curl directly to edge LB to force region selection header
  curl -sS -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" -H "X-Canary: canary-3" ... https://edge01.eu-west-1.redwood.test/v1/chat -D -

  Response headers showed: x-routing-eval: policy-v5, x-selected-pool: canary-pool-3, x-fallback-trigger: true

- tcpdump on edge01 (10s capture) to confirm backend connections
  sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/edge01-0903.pcap port 443 and host 10.200.1.45

  Looked for SYN/ACK delays to us-east backends: saw 120ms RTT to us-east-1 pool (expected 80ms), suggesting transient network blip.

Runtime logs (serving-runtime) (grep'ed)
  [2026-03-09T09:37:13Z] INFO routing eval=policy-v5 user=acct-123 route=/v1/chat selected=canary-pool-3 decision=[weight:0.12, fallback_on_error:true]
  [2026-03-09T09:37:13Z] WARN pool canary-pool-3: capacity-pressure high, inflight=342, queued=48
  [2026-03-09T09:37:14Z] ERROR modelserve us-east-1/redwood-v1-chat-q4_0: kv-cache-miss cold-start latency=850ms
  [2026-03-09T09:37:15Z] ERROR gateway: upstream response timeout after 30s

Edge LB debug
  - edge config snapshot (loaded at 09:20 UTC) shows canary rule with match: header X-Experiment=canary-3 and weight 0.0. But the policy-synced config says weight 0.12 (different source). Possible race between config service and canary controller.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Canary controller bug: staged rollout handler incorrectly applied weight delta early to some LB nodes (config drift). Evidence: mismatch between snapshot and policy store + some nodes had weight 0.12.
2) Network flakiness from eu-west-1->us-east-1 increased RTT and triggered fallback policy earlier than expected. Evidence: tcpdump RTT spike and canary pool reporting capacity pressure.
3) Model variant mismatch: fallback selected a quantized model variant (q4_0) without prewarmed KV cache, causing timeouts and 502/504. Evidence: runtime log kv-cache-miss and longer modelserve latencies.
4) Client header propagation issue: some clients had malformed X-Region headers causing unexpected routing decisions (low confidence).

Quick repro steps for engineering (what I did, can repeat)
- curl with X-Canary:X to edge01 to simulate matching canary header.
- ssh to edge01, tail /var/log/edge/route-eval.log and /var/log/edge/config-sync.log while toggling canary weight in staging policy service.
- run policy-sim tool (./policy-sim) with the same user profile to see how policy-v5 evaluates. Sample command:
  ./policy-sim --input ./case_eu_user.json --policy policy-v5 --log-level debug

Notes about policy-sim output
- For one sample user, policy-sim returned: {decision: "route-canary", weight: 0.12, fallback_on_error: true}
- policy-sim pointed to config-store://policies/policy-v5#commit-7b2e as source. That commit was updated by PR 256 (linked above) earlier today.

Mitigations attempted during event (and results)
- scaled up canary-pool-3 by +20 instances (SRE action): reduced queued from 48 -> 12 within 90s, but latency for fallback remained high because fallback triggered to us-east with cold caches.
- temporarily set canary weight to 0 on policy service for eu-west majority nodes: decreased canary traffic and errors normalized after ~4m.
- warmed q4_0 variant in us-east pool (preload prompts): reduced subsequent kv-cache misses.

What I still need to validate (TODO)
- trace which config sync order caused some edges to have 0.12 while snapshot at 09:20 had 0.0. Check config-sync logs (edge nodes) for 09:20-09:37 window.
- validate whether PR 256 included an unintended default weight. Look at the PR patchset and the rollout script used by product.
- confirm whether the fallback policy should prefer local unquantized variant before cross-region fallback; current docs say fallback priority = [local-variant, regional-variant, cross-region]. Logs imply cross-region happened first.
- reproduce locally: run a small simulated rollout with a canary weight bump from 0.0->0.12 across 10 nodes to see if race is reproducible.

Notes-to-self on instrumentation we lack
- We don't have a quick map from config-store commit -> nodes that loaded it (need per-node config-load hashes in telemetry). Adding that would make this class of bug easier.
- Need a metric that correlates "kv-cache-warmness" per-variant per-region (percentage of requests served from warmed cache vs cold-start).

Follow-ups for postmortem
- Owners: platform-routing (root cause analysis), serving-runtime (kv-cache behavior), infra-network (investigate RTT spike).
- Action items: add per-node config hash telemetry; add prewarm step to fallback policy for quantized variants; add guard in rollout controller to prevent partial application of weight to fewer than N nodes.

Raw snippets I copied into incident ticket
- "routing eval=policy-v5 ... selected=canary-pool-3 decision=[weight:0.12, fallback_on_error:true]"
- "ERROR modelserve us-east-1/redwood-v1-chat-q4_0: kv-cache-miss cold-start latency=850ms"
- tcpdump: "09:37:13.512 IP 10.200.1.45.443 > 10.0.5.12.56784: Flags [S.], seq 423423, ack 234234, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0"

Personal notes
- Marco thinks this smells like config-store race; Lena flagged the PR that touched default-canary-weight earlier today. Ping both.
- Keep the reproduction simple: don't need full traffic, just 10 nodes with simulated client headers.

Done list (what I closed during incident)
- lowered canary weight to 0 (temporary)
- scaled canary pool + prewarmed q4_0 in fallback region
- opened JIRA-RI-4982 and linked PR 256 for review

If I forget: next step is to run the policy-sim across a matrix of (node-load, network-latency, canary-weight) to find threshold where partial application occurs. Add results to the postmortem doc.

END
